lines: How did the Dutch turn a sea into a lake?
The Zy-der-zee was a salty bay, open to the North Sea.
From 1927, up to 10,000 workers piled sand and clay across it.
On 28 May 1932, they closed the last gap.
Cut off from the sea and fed by rivers, the water slowly turned fresh. The Eye-sel-meer.
Twenty-five sluices still drain it to the sea at low tide.
One wall. That's how the Dutch turned a sea into a lake.
